consumer: mission::is_complete for MGOAL_FIND_ITEM, asking 'does the player's crafting_inventory hold item_count of type->item_id (or charges)?' to decide if the fetch objective is met.
scope: items reachable for crafting (carried plus nearby reachable inventory via crafting_inventory()), not just on-person carried items
decisive_source: src/mission.cpp::mission::is_complete (MGOAL_FIND_ITEM) — its body builds u.crafting_inventory() and returns whether tmp_inv.has_amount(item_id,item_count) (or has_amount>=1 && has_charges) is satisfied, i.e. it EVALUATES the objective-met yes/no.
divergence: The required parts sit on an adjacent reachable tile (in crafting reach but not carried): an on-person-only possession check or a read of the snapshot's carried items reports 'not met' while the engine's is_complete reports met — wrong-reach predicate exposed.
